headline: ICT orders Sheikh Hasina and 29 others to appear on Sept 16
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has directed authorities to publish notices for the ousted prime minister and other high-profile figures accused in the 2013 crackdown.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has ordered the publication of notices in two newspapers asking ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed to appear before it on September 16.
The order comes after the prosecution informed the tribunal that 30 accused persons, including Hasina, could not be found at their respective addresses.
The case relates to the 2013 crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka and in Narayanganj on May 5-6.

The tribunal had previously issued arrest warrants against the absconding accused. On July 27, formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity were accepted against Sheikh Hasina, two journalists, and 38 others.
If the accused fail to appear or cannot be traced, the tribunal will appoint state-appointed lawyers to represent them and conduct the defence based on provided documents.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina and 29 others must appear before the International Crimes Tribunal on September 16.

The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has ordered the publication of notices in two newspapers asking ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed to appear before it on September 16.

The order comes after the prosecution informed the tribunal that 30 accused persons, including Hasina, could not be found at their respective addresses.

The case relates to the 2013 crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka and in Narayanganj on May 5-6.

The tribunal had previously issued arrest warrants against the absconding accused. On July 27, formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity were accepted against Sheikh Hasina, two journalists, and 38 others.

If the accused fail to appear or cannot be traced, the tribunal will appoint state-appointed lawyers to represent them and conduct the defence based on provided documents.

headline_marked: 18 killed as [[US and Iran exchange biggest strikes]] since July
headline: 18 killed as US and Iran exchange biggest strikes since July
summary: Washington hit Iran's southern coast while Tehran targeted US bases across the Middle East, sparking fears of a full-scale regional war.
details: The United States and Iran have engaged in their most significant exchange of fire since July, with Washington striking Iran's southern coast and Tehran targeting US bases in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, and Iraq.

Iran's health minister reported that 18 people were killed and 108 injured in the latest US strikes. This includes a reported attack on a wedding party in Sirik County, where four people, including a 4-year-old, were killed.

The US military stated it targeted air defenses, radar systems, maritime assets, and communications sites. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins denied targeting civilians, attributing reports of civilian casualties to Iranian state media.

In retaliation, Iran launched missile and drone attacks on US assets, including the Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait. While Iran claimed to have killed US forces in Jordan and Iraq, US officials stated there were no casualties based on initial assessments.

President Donald Trump stated that the US hit Iran 'very hard' and expressed readiness to launch further strikes at any time. He also asserted that the Strait of Hormuz remains open to shipping despite the tensions.

The conflict threatens global energy supplies, as the Strait of Hormuz handles 20% of global oil and LNG shipments. Iran has blacklisted 56 ships, threatening fines or confiscation if they sail without Tehran's permission.

Local residents in southern Iranian port cities like Bandar Abbas expressed fear that the escalation signals a return to full-scale war, describing the recent attacks as feeling like 'the end of the world'.
